key_decisions.ma_choice: gnt is combinational from req plus registered mask_q, owner_q and lock_q. There is no pipeline stage on req->gnt.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D1: gnt is combinational in the same cycle from req, lock and registered pointer, owner and counter.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Registered thermometer mask with masked and unmasked lowest-set-bit selects; the masked result wins if any masked request is present.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D4: dual masked/unmasked fixed-priority encoders with a registered thermometer mask.

key_decisions.ma_choice: x & (~x+1) using a carry-lookahead increment as the baseline. A Kogge-Stone prefix-OR is the fallback if timing fails.
key_decisions.plan_choice: A log-depth prefix-OR find-first from the start.
key_decisions.note: The plan starts from the MA's fallback option. The architecture is unchanged.

key_decisions.ma_choice: The mask moves past the winner only on a fresh arbitration. It is held during locked continuation and when no request is present.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D5: the pointer updates to the granted index on every grant, including continuations, and holds when idle.
key_decisions.note: During a continuation the granted index equals the owner, which the mask already points past, so the resulting state is identical.

key_decisions.ma_choice: lock_req = |(gnt&lock&req) is registered together with owner_q. The owner is granted while lock_q and req[owner] hold. If the owner drops req, the lock is released and RR runs in the same cycle. A lock without a grant is ignored.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D6: the same equations and the same same-cycle fallback.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Only continuation cycles are counted, so a burst is at most MAX_LOCK+1 grants. Setting the parameter to L-1 includes the first cycle.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D7: continuation-only counting, burst of MAX_LOCK+1, with the L-1 guidance.

key_decisions.ma_choice: The lock is cleared and the next cycle re-arbitrates with the owner at lowest priority. The arbiter is work-conserving, so the owner can be re-granted immediately if it is alone.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D7: release at expiry, former owner lowest priority, immediate re-grant via RR if alone.

key_decisions.ma_choice: The counter is unused; LCNT_W is forced to 1 and the timeout term is disabled.
key_decisions.plan_choice: A generate-if removes the counter when MAX_LOCK=0.
key_decisions.note: The functional intent is the same.

key_decisions.ma_choice: gnt_locked = locked_now, which is high only on continuation cycles.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D9: high only on lock-override cycles, low on the initial grant.

key_decisions.ma_choice: gnt_id comes combinationally from an OR-tree one-hot-to-binary encoder and is 0 when invalid. gnt_valid = |gnt.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D3 and S6: combinational and cycle-aligned, index 0 when invalid, valid = |gnt.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Worst case is (N-1)*(MAX_LOCK+1) cycles. With MAX_LOCK=0 the bound depends on masters releasing their locks.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D8: R11 is conditional when MAX_LOCK=0. The plan re-derives (N-1)*(MAX_LOCK+1) and flags the user's (N-1)*MAX_LOCK as a discrepancy.
key_decisions.note: The plan reaches the correct bound rather than adopting the user's figure.

key_decisions.ma_choice: No ack input; every grant cycle counts as served. A gnt_ack input is listed as an open extension.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D2: no accept/ready input; every grant counts as served.

key_decisions.decision: Reset state and grant gating during reset
key_decisions.ma_choice: mask_q resets to all 1s, giving requester 0 first priority. gnt is ANDed with rst_n so it is forced to 0 during reset. Deassertion is synchronised externally.
key_decisions.note: The plan has requester 0 first priority and external reset synchronisation (D11). It never forces combinational gnt to 0 while rst_n is low, so gnt can assert during reset.

key_decisions.decision: Timing budget for the combinational path
key_decisions.ma_choice: About 60% of the 2 ns cycle goes to the arbiter. The critical path is req->increment->AND->mux->gnt, at 6-8 levels for N=16.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D10: about 50% (1 ns) of the cycle, with critical path req->masked PE->select->lock mux->gnt->index.
key_decisions.note: Only the budget split assumption differs.

summary: The plan closely tracks the reference MA. It matches on the zero-latency combinational grant, the dual masked/unmasked priority scheme, lock capture and release with same-cycle fallback, continuation-only MAX_LOCK counting, expiry behaviour, locked-flag semantics, combinational index/valid outputs, the no-backpressure default and the (N-1)*(MAX_LOCK+1) starvation bound. The plan corrected the user's (N-1)*MAX_LOCK bound to reach that figure. Three differences are equivalent: updating the pointer on every grant rather than only on fresh arbitration (same resulting state), starting from a prefix-OR find-first rather than x&-x, and a 50% rather than 60% timing budget. The only omission is forcing combinational gnt to 0 during reset. Q1 was largely needless: R6 already says lock is asserted with req while granted, and R3/R4 imply the same-cycle fallback with no bubble. Q2 and Q3 resolved genuine ambiguities.
